study type: Quasi-experimental cohort study (before and after protocol change)
outcome: Duration of central venous catheter placement
Time to achieve full enteral feeding
cohort: All very low-birth-weight infants admitted on their first postnatal day in a neonatal intensive care unit during two 12-month periods (before and after a feeding protocol change).
finding: The implementation of a fast enteral feeding progression protocol for very low-birth-weight infants significantly decreased the central venous catheter duration and time to achieve full enteral feeding, with no increase in late-onset sepsis or necrotising enterocolitis rates.
birth_weight: Median 980 g (SD 300 g), Very low-birth-weight infants
